memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Do not mistreat or oppress a foreigner, for you were foreigners in Egypt." - Exodus 22:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives His people a reason as well as a command: do not mistreat the foreigner, because you know exactly what it feels like to be one. Israel had lived as strangers in Egypt, vulnerable and oppressed. Now that they had their own land, God would not let them become oppressors in turn. Their own painful history was meant to make them tender toward the outsider, not hard.

This is a beautiful principle for the heart. God often takes our hardest experiences and turns them into wells of compassion for others. The grief you have known can make you gentle with the grieving. The loneliness you have felt can make you welcoming to the lonely. What broke you can become the very thing that lets you comfort others (2 Cor 1:4). Our God wastes no pain.

At its core, this command flows from the character of God, who has a special heart for the outsider, the stranger, the one who does not belong. And this is our own story too — we were once strangers, far from God, without hope in the world. Yet in Christ we have been brought near and made members of His family (Eph 2:19). Having been welcomed by such grace, how can we do anything but welcome others? Look around today for the outsider God may be asking you to embrace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Who around me feels like an outsider that God may be calling me to welcome?
How has God used my own hard experiences to grow compassion in me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You welcomed me when I was a stranger far from You. Give me Your heart for the outsider and the overlooked, and let my own pain become compassion for others. Amen.
